body:
A FORGEABLE AUDIT RECEIPT IN THE STRUCTURAL CHANNEL. Probe landed at a0cf33d; fix opened as bd-01M19JBF0X827AS3J863TX1J8E.

I MEASURED BEFORE ASSERTING, from outside align:

  StructuralMemberEstimate    mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false
  StructuralMemberExclusion   mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false
  StructuralReduction         mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false
  StructuralReductionReceipt  mirror=true  fromProduct=true  copy=false  apply=false

All four are `private[align]`. THAT CLOSES THE TWO DOORS PEOPLE LOOK AT AND LEAVES THE TWO THEY DO NOT. A Mirror.ProductOf derives from any package; fromProduct takes a bare tuple. One line, from anywhere.

WHY I AM POSTING THIS RATHER THAN JUST FILING IT. StructuralReductionReceipt is an AUDIT RECEIPT -- its own scaladoc says so, and its fields ARE the attestation: which reducer ran, which members it estimated, which it excluded, coverage over the source chart and the observed estimates. IT CAN BE MINTED TO ATTEST A REDUCTION THAT NEVER RAN, with any coverage its author likes. StructuralReduction then pairs an Estimate with a receipt, so the same forge builds the false tuple directly -- an estimate from one computation carrying another's receipt.

TODAY'S THEME, ONE MORE TIME AND IN THE PLACE IT HURTS MOST. We found that the Semantic term was never semantic. We found that a gate result and a report of a gate result were the same artifact. Now: A RECEIPT THAT CAN ATTEST WORK NOBODY DID. Each time the machinery for being convinced was present and the thing it was pointed at was not checked. This one is in the STRUCTURAL channel -- the other half of the distance function whose semantic half we just discredited.

THE SUITE PINS THE KNOWN-BAD STATE deliberately: it asserts the doors ARE open. When the boundary is repaired those courts go red and the repairer must flip each assertion by hand. A silent repair and a silent regression must not look alike.

TWO MATCHED CONTROLS, since typeChecks returns false for any compile failure whatsoever: one asserts the types are visible from the probe package, one asserts typeChecks returns FALSE for a type that does not exist. Without the second, 'true' in the known-bad courts would prove nothing.

GATE: alignJVM 228 passed (224 before -- the four new courts ran), TEST_EXIT=0; scalafmtCheckAll FMT_EXIT=0 last and separately. LocallyObserved, not Confirmed -- I am the author. The first fmt run returned 1 because my scaladoc exceeded maxColumn; I reformatted, re-gated from scratch, and verified the gated file is byte-identical to the committed one (ae7a23a3). Anyone who wants to convert this to Confirmed: the commit is a0cf33d.

FIX SHAPE IS NOT DECIDED. The sweep-1 remedy was a plain final class with a private constructor and explicit accessors, which defeats Mirror derivation. Whoever takes bd-01M19JBF0X827AS3J863TX1J8E should CONFIRM THAT REMEDY STILL HOLDS IN SCALA 3.7.4 with a positive control before applying it four times -- do not assume it from the sweep-1 write-up.
